use: The everyday word for any meal: asagohan, hirugohan and bangohan are breakfast, lunch and dinner.

example.romaji: issho ni gohan tabe ni ikou yo
example.ja: 一緒にご飯食べに行こうよ
example.english: Let's go get something to eat together.

examplePolite.romaji: issho ni gohan tabe ni ikimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 一緒にご飯食べに行きませんか?
examplePolite.english: Would you like to go and eat together?

notes: Also plain cooked rice: gohan o taku means cook the rice.

use: A step more formal than gohan; common in invitations, at restaurants and in health talk.

example.ja: 今度食事でもどう?
example.english: How about dinner sometime?

examplePolite.romaji: kondo oshokuji demo ikaga desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今度お食事でもいかがですか?
examplePolite.english: Would you like to have dinner sometime?

notes: Shokuji suru means to have a meal. Oshokuji is the polite form for someone else's meal.

use: Rough word for gohan, used mostly by men among friends.

example.ja: 腹減った、飯行こうぜ
example.english: I'm starving, let's go eat.

notes: Also heard in hirumeshi (lunch) and yorumeshi (dinner). Say gohan yourself unless you're among close friends.

use: Used for kinds of food, as in favourite foods or foods you can't eat.

example.ja: 好きな食べ物は何?
example.english: What's your favourite food?

examplePolite.romaji: suki na tabemono wa nan desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 好きな食べ物は何ですか?

example.ja: 飲み物は何にする?
example.english: What do you want to drink?

examplePolite.romaji: nomimono wa nani ni shimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 飲み物は何にしますか?
examplePolite.english: What would you like to drink?

notes: Staff say onomimono: 'onomimono wa?' asks for your drink order.

use: On its own it means Japanese green tea; black tea is koucha.

example.ja: ちょっとお茶でも飲もうか
example.english: Shall we grab a cup of tea?

examplePolite.ja: ちょっとお茶でも飲みませんか?
examplePolite.english: Would you like to grab a cup of tea?

notes: Ocha suru means going to a cafe for a drink, whatever you order.

example.romaji: asa wa itsumo koohii nomu yo
example.ja: 朝はいつもコーヒー飲むよ
example.english: I always have coffee in the morning.

examplePolite.romaji: asa wa itsumo koohii o nomimasu
examplePolite.ja: 朝はいつもコーヒーを飲みます
examplePolite.english: I always have coffee in the morning.

notes: Iced coffee is aisu koohii; a hot one is hotto.

use: The polite way to say mizu; what you ask for at a restaurant.

example.ja: ちょっとお水もらってもいい?
example.english: Can I get some water?

examplePolite.ja: すみません、お水をください
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, could I have some water?

notes: Mizu is always cold or room-temperature water, never hot.

use: Japanese has its own word for hot water; don't say atsui mizu.

example.ja: ちょっとお湯沸かしてくれる?
example.english: Can you boil some water?

examplePolite.romaji: chotto oyu o wakashite moraemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: ちょっとお湯を沸かしてもらえますか?

notes: Oyu o wakasu means boil water. Also the hot water in a bath.

example.romaji: kyou wa niku ga tabetai na
example.ja: 今日は肉が食べたいな
example.english: I feel like eating meat today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa niku ga tabetai desu
examplePolite.ja: 今日は肉が食べたいです
examplePolite.english: I'd like to eat meat today.

notes: Beef is gyuuniku, pork butaniku, chicken toriniku.

example.romaji: sakana anmari suki ja nai n da
example.ja: 魚あんまり好きじゃないんだ
example.english: I'm not really into fish.

examplePolite.romaji: sakana wa amari suki ja nai n desu
examplePolite.ja: 魚はあまり好きじゃないんです

example.ja: 野菜もちゃんと食べてね
example.english: Make sure you eat your vegetables too.

examplePolite.romaji: yasai mo chanto tabete kudasai ne
examplePolite.ja: 野菜もちゃんと食べてくださいね
examplePolite.english: Please make sure you eat your vegetables too.

example.ja: 果物なら何が好き?
example.english: What fruit do you like?

examplePolite.romaji: kudamono nara nani ga suki desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 果物なら何が好きですか?

notes: Furuutsu is also used, mostly for desserts and drinks.

example.romaji: ashita yasumi da kara asobi ni ikou yo
example.ja: 明日休みだから遊びに行こうよ
example.english: I'm off tomorrow, let's go out.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita wa yasumi na node asobi ni ikimashou
examplePolite.ja: 明日は休みなので遊びに行きましょう
examplePolite.english: I'm off tomorrow, so let's go out.

notes: Natsuyasumi is the summer holiday, hiruyasumi the lunch break. The verb is yasumu.

use: Short for arubaito; the usual word for students' jobs and side jobs.

example.ja: 今日バイトあるから無理
example.english: I can't today, I've got work.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa baito ga aru node muri desu
examplePolite.ja: 今日はバイトがあるので無理です
examplePolite.english: I can't today because I have my part-time job.

example.romaji: kongetsu, kyuuryou chotto sukunakatta n da
example.ja: 今月、給料ちょっと少なかったんだ
example.english: My pay was a bit low this month.

examplePolite.romaji: kongetsu wa kyuuryou ga chotto sukunakatta n desu
examplePolite.ja: 今月は給料がちょっと少なかったんです
examplePolite.english: My pay was a little low this month.

notes: Kyuuryoubi is payday. Kyuuryou ga agaru means get a raise.

use: Covers bread, rolls and sweet buns.

example.romaji: asa wa pan to koohii dake
example.ja: 朝はパンとコーヒーだけ
example.english: Just bread and coffee for breakfast.

examplePolite.romaji: asa wa pan to koohii dake desu
examplePolite.ja: 朝はパンとコーヒーだけです
examplePolite.english: I just have bread and coffee for breakfast.

example.romaji: tamago ato futatsu shika nai yo
example.ja: 卵あと二つしかないよ
example.english: We've only got two eggs left.

examplePolite.romaji: tamago ga ato futatsu shika arimasen
examplePolite.ja: 卵があと二つしかありません
examplePolite.english: There are only two eggs left.

notes: Tamagoyaki is rolled omelette; nama tamago is raw egg, often eaten on rice.

use: Cow's milk you drink or buy; miruku is more for milk in coffee and for babies.

example.ja: 牛乳切れてるから買ってきて
example.english: We're out of milk, can you go buy some?

examplePolite.romaji: gyuunyuu ga kirete iru node katte kite kudasai
examplePolite.ja: 牛乳が切れているので買ってきてください
examplePolite.english: We're out of milk, so please go buy some.

example.ja: チーズのせたらおいしいよ
example.english: It's really good with cheese on top.

examplePolite.romaji: chiizu o nosetara oishii desu yo
examplePolite.ja: チーズをのせたらおいしいですよ
examplePolite.english: It's delicious with cheese on top.

notes: Also what you say for a photo: hai, chiizu.
